message.content:
Driving from San Francisco to Los Angeles typically covers about **380–400 miles** (≈ 610–640 km) along the I‑5 corridor.  
If you maintain an average speed of roughly **60 mph** (the legal limit on most of the freeway), the trip would take around **6½–7 hours**.

In practice, actual travel time varies:

| Factor | Effect on Time |
|--------|----------------|
| **Traffic congestion** (especially near the Bay Area, Sacramento, and the Los Angeles metro) | Adds 30 min–2 hrs, depending on time of day |
| **Stops / breaks** (fuel, food, rest) | Adds 15–30 min per stop |
| **Roadwork / detours** | Can add 10–30 min or more if major closures |

So, a realistic estimate for a typical weekday drive is **6–8 hours**, while weekend or off‑peak trips may be closer to **6 hours**. If you’re planning a trip, it’s wise to check real‑time traffic updates (e.g., Google Maps, Waze) before you leave.
